intent: The panel its Collapsible shows while open and hides while closed, animating its height between the two.
typical_uses: The body of a Collapsible, revealed when the user opens it

dont_use_when.situation: The body of one of several headed sections

invariants.text: Once its close transition ends, a closed panel is removed from the DOM. With `keepMounted` it stays in the DOM under the `hidden` attribute; with `hiddenUntilFound` it stays as `hidden="until-found"`, so the browser's find-in-page can match its text and ask to open it - the root's `onOpenChange` is called with true, and an uncontrolled root opens. `hiddenUntilFound` overrides `keepMounted`.

Open and close animate the panel's height between 0 and Base UI's `--collapsible-panel-height`, a measurement the primitive writes on the panel element, not a theme token; the transition is 200ms and is turned off under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`.
The panel always has `overflow: hidden`, open or closed, so anything a descendant draws outside the panel's box (a focus outline at its edge, a negative margin) is clipped.

anti_patterns.dont: Put form controls whose values must survive a collapse in a panel without `keepMounted`
anti_patterns.do_instead: Set `keepMounted` (or `hiddenUntilFound`) on the panel, or hold the values in state outside it - an unmounted panel takes its uncontrolled inputs' values and focus with it

a11y.by: The primitive's Collapsible.Panel puts the id the trigger's `aria-controls` names on the panel and the `hidden` attribute on it while closed and kept mounted; collapsible.test.tsx asserts the panel is absent from the DOM until opened and again after a second click

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the panel's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - the compiler emits one JSON type per property.

style.states: style accepts a function of the panel's state as well as a plain style object
style.because: Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (open, disabled, transitionStatus). The compiler emits one JSON type per property, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through collapsible.module.css, not through this.

good.title: A panel that keeps its inputs across a collapse
A panel the browser's find-in-page can open

bad.title: A panel with no Collapsible around it
bad.why: CollapsibleContent reads the nearest Collapsible's open state through Base UI context and throws when there is none, so it cannot render on its own.
